title: A finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a product of henselian local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $R\to B$ a ring map making $B$ a finitely generated $R$-module. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$, local rings $(B_1,\mathfrak n_1),\dots,(B_r,\mathfrak n_r)$, each an $R$-algebra and a finitely generated $R$-module, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $B\cong B_1\times\dots\times B_r$ ($B=0$ if $r=0$), such that for every $i$: $B_i$ is a henselian local ring, and $R\to B_i$ is a local homomorphism ($\mathfrak n_i\cap R=\mathfrak m$, the preimage of $\mathfrak n_i$ in $R$ being $\mathfrak m$), so that $B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ is a finite field extension of $\kappa$.
